purpose: Inventory of Google Flow runtime dependencies classified for the Stage A migration (Phase 2 hard removal). Classification: DELETE (Flow-only), MIGRATE (shared value moved to engine-neutral services), KEEP_GENERAL (shared capability, NOT Flow), HISTORICAL_ONLY (archived evidence/docs).

scope_definition.google_flow_runtime: tools/windagent_tools/google_flow/ (browser adapter for the Google Flow generative-video web UI)
scope_definition.not_in_scope: Google Gemini model provider (providers/windagent_providers/google/) is a general LLM provider and MUST NOT be removed; it shares only the word 'google'.

DELETE: tools/windagent_tools/google_flow/ (entire package: __init__, candidate_downloader, human_control, image_generation, image_operations, job_record, navigation, pre_submit_guard, project_manager, review_approval, selectors/, state_machine, video_candidates, video_generation, video_inspection, video_operations) — ~1200+ LOC, all Flow-specific
tools/windagent_tools/video_probe.py Flow imports (module itself may be kept; its google_flow import must be removed)

tools/windagent_tools/__init__.py Flow re-exports (FlowImageGenerator, FlowVideoGenerator, FlowJobRegistry, FlowNavigator, FlowProjectManager, FlowUiState, FlowImageOperation, FlowVideoOperation, VideoCandidateDownloader)

MIGRATE.item: FlowGenerationSpecification + prompt compiler (core prompt_compiler.py, intelligence prompt_compiler/modes.py, director/prompts.py generation_mode block)
MIGRATE.to: IR creative_prompt separation; legacy compiler becomes a bounded compatibility layer with a sunset date

MIGRATE.item: Idempotency / cancellation / retry / artifact hash / provenance / fail-closed review guarantees inside Flow adapters
Flow-specific browser navigation state machines (state_machine, navigation, project_manager)
MIGRATE.to: retired; generic BrowserRuntime remains as the shared agent browser capability

KEEP_GENERAL: tools/windagent_tools/browser/ (BrowserRuntime, action policy, state encryption, session locks) — shared agent capability
core MediaGenerationProviderPort (contract remains; GenerationRequest loses generation_mode coupling over time)
TTS/audio pipeline, post-production, storage, verification, observability layers
HISTORICAL_ONLY: historical verification evidence referencing Flow (artifacts/video_production/* flow evidence)
Flow selector maps / DOM catalogs (google_flow/selectors) if archived for provenance, never re-imported

DELETE: docs/video_production/flow_* (current-release runtime contracts for Flow adapters)
docs/video_production/browser_runtime/* only if Flow-specific; browser_runtime_contract.md and browser_action_policy.md are KEEP_GENERAL (shared browser capability)
HISTORICAL_ONLY: old roadmap artifacts describing the Google Flow provider (road_map.md rewrite supersedes them)

MIGRATE: tests exercising idempotency/cancellation/retry/hash/provenance semantics — rewritten against fake ProductionEnginePort + IR fixtures

DELETE: Flow browser session credentials, Flow project URLs, Flow-specific env keys (none committed; scan required at removal)

inbound_domain_concepts: core GenerationMode enum -> Shot.generation_mode, ShotSpecification.generation_mode, GenerationModeDecision, FlowGenerationSpecification, GenerationRequest.generation_mode
outbound: google_flow/* imports only within-package modules + windagent_tools.browser (runtime/agent_browser/state) + windagent_core domain/ids/events
google_flow NEVER imports storage/ORM; it is a pure browser adapter (phase 13/14 architecture constraint)

browser_shared_boundary.note: BrowserRuntime (tools/windagent_tools/browser/runtime.py) is a durable, bounded browser worker used by the whole agent. Only the Flow-specific navigation/project/selectors logic on top of it is DELETE. browser_runtime_contract.md docs remain.

migration_contract.compatibility_window: Stage A in full (Phases 0-2). During the window the legacy GenerationRequest/FlowGenerationSpecification path stays readable; the IR becomes the source of truth for new productions.
migration_contract.schema_versioning: ProductionIrDocument schema_version 1.0.0 (MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH, fail-closed on unknown MAJOR, additive fields allowed within MAJOR 1) — reuses the VideoProductionPackage versioning policy.
migration_contract.event_migration: Legacy VideoProductionEventCatalog remains for historical streams; new ProductionIrEventCatalog (video_production_ir.*) is additive. No dual-write beyond the compatibility window.
migration_contract.rollback: IR is purely additive in Phase 1; rollback = stop emitting IR documents and keep consuming VideoProductionPackage v1. No persisted schema is migrated destructively in Phase 1.
removal_conditions_for_google_flow: 1. Composition root / workflow / API / UI consume ProductionEnginePort + IR schemas (Phase 2 items 1-2).
2. `rg google_flow` and `rg 'FlowVideo|FlowImage|flow_video'` return zero runtime references (historical archive allowlist only).
3. Architecture test forbidding Flow imports from canonical packages passes.
4. Config/secret validator reports zero Flow residue.
5. Full regression not below baseline outside the retirement manifest.
migration_contract.data_risk: GenerationRequest is referenced by storage/workflow; persisted data must be read via the migrator during the window. No destructive migration of persisted generation_records.
